rites.name: Ryalleneth
rites.text: Ryalleneth is the concept of the first hard resolve in Gouthun, the note that held when the Singing settled roots into the young world. Her presence is said to steady loose matter during the Age of Sundering, when landfall tore old bonds apart.

rites.name: Telausialor
rites.text: Telausialor is the concept of a binding oath sworn before the Courts, the principle by which a trial's verdict becomes law across the doors between worlds. In the Age of Sundering it was the force that held councils together when landfall tore old alliances apart.

rites.name: Brurdane
rites.text: Brurdane is a concept of Gouthun's Seeding, the quiet season when makers plant the Weave and dormant powers rest beneath the groves. It names the stillness that gathers over growing kingdoms in the Age of the first sovereign.

rites.name: Osulaari
rites.text: Osulaari is the concept of the Weave, the planted lattice of power that the makers set into the soil of Gouthun during the Seeding. In the Holy Age its temples and orders taught that quiet powers could be woken by flame and disciplined ritual.

rites.name: Venioneila
rites.text: Venioneila is a concept of Gouthun's Martial Realm, born in the Fall when the old worlds cracked and the Shards scattered across the sky. It is remembered as the will that held the broken fragments together long enough for the Pact to be sworn among the surviving peoples.

rites.name: Ilokaoma
rites.text: Ilokaoma is a concept of the Walled Age in Gouthun, a discipline of holding ground and bearing weight that the orders of the walls taught for centuries. Its practitioners are known for first crossings, where a single defended threshold is opened for the first time by sustained will. It is remembered as the art that made the walls endure.

rites.name: Elirlys
rites.text: Elirlys is the concept of a shield-grammar in Gouthun's Walled Age, the discipline by which holding walls were raised and renewed across centuries. Its orders taught that a wall is a promise kept by repetition, and first crossings were made wherever that promise was tested. It was carried through the groves and growing kingdoms of the first sovereign's reign.

rites.name: Isevsora
rites.text: Isevsora is a concept of the Walled Age in Gouthun, a discipline of holding walls and vowed orders that kept the first crossings from breaking old bonds. Its practitioners stood at the seams of settled land during the Age of Sundering, when landfall reshaped every border.
